# Owen Ford

- **Age:** presumed thirty or thirty-five  <sub>[v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen Ford is a tall, broad-shouldered man with thick, brown hair. His countenance features a finely-cut nose and chin, as well as large, brilliant dark-gray eyes.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008)_

## Personality

Owen Ford possesses a pleasant voice, a delightful smile, and a keen sense of style. Around thirty or thirty-five years old, he is motivated by the ambition to write a great Canadian novel.

## History

Owen Ford was a newspaper writer and magazine short-story author who traveled to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) to recover from a spring bout of typhoid fever and find inspiration for a novel. After meeting [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and boarding at [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) Moore's house, he visited Captain Jim, who shared his treasured life-book and inspired Owen to write a novel based on the captain's life and tales. Throughout a summer spent writing the manuscript alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), and Captain Jim, Owen fell deeply in love with [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), though he initially agonized over leaving her behind due to her circumstances. Upon returning to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) for a visit, Owen declared his love to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) in the garden, and she confessed her love for him in return, receiving a heartwarming benediction from Captain Jim.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P1](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0001), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P17](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0017), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), +20 more_

## Quotes

> "Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?"
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)

> "You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)

> "but in the main it’s done. I wrote the last sentence this morning. If I can find a publisher for it it will probably be out next summer or fall."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P19](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0019)

> "Yes—love triumphant and perfect. Leslie, you know—you understand. I have loved you from the first. And I KNOW you love me—I don’t need to ask you. But I want to hear you say it—my darling—my darling!"
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)

> "But he must often be lonely. There was a touch of the seer about him tonight—he spoke as one to whom it had been given to speak. Well, I must be going, too."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES P26](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0026)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--owen-ford.md)

[Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and Owen are close friends and correspondents who bonded while walking through [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) and visiting local sites together. Owen confided his deep romantic agony over [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), who offered him sympathy and urged him to respect the situation before later encouraging the pair's happiness. [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) also supported Owen's literary efforts as he worked to adapt Captain Jim's life story into a novel.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P1](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0001), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P17](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0017), +19 more_

### [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/leslie-moore--owen-ford.md)

Owen was immediately struck by Leslie's beauty when he arrived to board at the Moore household, and he quickly fell deeply in love with her during a summer spent writing a novel together. Though he initially agonized over leaving her due to her difficult circumstances, he eventually returned to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) and declared his love in the garden. [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) confessed her love in return, establishing their mutual romantic commitment.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P1](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0001), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P17](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0017), +18 more_

### [Susan](../character/susan.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/owen-ford--susan.md)

### [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/owen-ford--uncle-jim.md)

Owen and Captain Jim shared a special connection after Captain Jim recognized Owen as the grandson of the schoolmaster's bride from his past. They became close literary collaborators when Owen agreed to turn the captain's treasured life-book and sea tales into a complete novel manuscript. Captain Jim bestowed a heartwarming benediction upon Owen and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) after the two declared their love for one another.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P10](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0010), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), +10 more_
